# STM32H743 Nano Flight Controller + 4-in-1 ESC (Job #46): Power-Stage and DShot Design Model

## 0. Scope and Assumptions

**Architecture.** On a 4-in-1 ESC, the STM32H743 is the flight controller MCU, running ArduPilot. Commutation and the 48 kHz PWM are generated by a separate ESC MCU running AM32 or BLHeli_32/Bluejay (e.g., STM32G071, AT32F421, or EFM8). The model below follows that split:

- **Power stage (×4):** loss and thermal model.
- **FC ↔ ESC link:** bidirectional DShot600, generated by H743 timers and DMA.

**Baseline parameters.** These are example values. Substitute your datasheet numbers; every equation stays parametric.

| Symbol | Meaning | Value |
|---|---|---|
| V_bus | 6S battery, full charge | 25.2 V |
| I_burst | Phase current per channel | 80 A, 5 s burst |
| f_sw | ESC PWM frequency | 48 kHz |
| R_ds(on),25 | MOSFET on-resistance at 25 °C, V_gs = 10 V (40 V class, 5×6 DFN) | 1.2 mΩ |
| α | R_ds(on) temperature coefficient | ≈ 0.4 %/K, so R(T) = R₂₅·(1 + α(T − 25)) |
| t_r, t_f | Switching edges at I_burst with the chosen gate resistance | 20 ns each |
| Q_rr | Body-diode reverse-recovery charge | 40 nC |
| C_oss | Output capacitance at V_bus | 1.5 nF |
| V_f | Body-diode forward drop | 0.8 V |
| t_dead | Dead time per edge | 100 ns |
| Q_g, V_drv | Gate charge and drive voltage | 50 nC, 10 V |
| Board | 4-layer copper stack | 37 × 37 mm, 6 × 2 oz layers, 1.6 mm FR-4 |

> **Reality check.** 80 A per channel on a nano (20×20 or 30.5 mm) 4-in-1 board is only a short burst rating. The board cannot sustain it, as shown in §3. Treat 80 A as a 1–5 s transient.

---

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

### 1.1 Six-step synchronous commutation

During any 60° commutation sector, one phase's high side is PWM'd at duty D. Its complementary low side conducts during (1 − D) through synchronous rectification. A second phase's low side conducts 100% of the time. At any instant, therefore, exactly two FETs carry the phase current I:

$$
P_{cond} = I^2 R_{hs} D + I^2 R_{ls}(1-D) + I^2 R_{ls} \approx 2\,I^2 R_{ds(on)}(T_j)
$$

This holds whenever R_hs ≈ R_ls, independent of D.

### 1.2 Temperature coupling (fixed-point iteration)

R_ds(on) depends on junction temperature, which depends on the loss. Solve iteratively:

$$
T_j^{(k+1)} = T_{board} + \frac{P_{FET}(T_j^{(k)})}{1}\,R_{\theta,j\text{-}b}, \quad R(T_j)=R_{25}[1+\alpha(T_j-25)]
$$

Convergence is guaranteed while 2I²R₂₅·α·R_θ < 1. At T_j ≈ 125 °C:

$$
R_{hot}=1.2\,\text{m}\Omega\,(1+0.004\cdot100)=1.68\,\text{m}\Omega
$$

$$
P_{cond}=2\cdot80^2\cdot1.68\times10^{-3}=\mathbf{21.5\ W\ per\ channel}
$$

Each FET conducts roughly one-third of each electrical cycle. Average dissipation per FET is about P_cond/3 ≈ 7.2 W, spread across the six FETs of the bridge.

### 1.3 Copper and shunt losses

Shunt, 0.5 mΩ: I²R = 3.2 W. This applies only if the shunt is in the phase path. A DC-bus shunt sees the current with PWM averaging instead.

Phase and bus copper, ~0.3 mΩ effective: about 1.9 W.

---

## 2. Switching Loss Model at 48 kHz

| Term | Equation | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Hard-switch V·I overlap | ½·V·I·(t_r + t_f)·f_sw | ½·25.2·80·40 ns·48 k = **1.94 W** |
| Reverse recovery | Q_rr·V·f_sw | 40 nC·25.2·48 k = **0.05 W** |
| C_oss discharge | ½·C_oss·V²·f_sw ×2 (both FETs in leg) | **0.05 W** |
| Dead-time diode conduction | V_f·I·2t_dead·f_sw | 0.8·80·200 ns·48 k = **0.61 W** |
| Gate drive (2 switching FETs) | 2·Q_g·V_drv·f_sw | **0.05 W** (dissipated in driver/R_g) |
| **P_sw total** | | **≈ 2.7 W per channel** |

**Design levers:**
- Switching loss scales linearly with f_sw. At 24 kHz it is about 1.4 W, but you pay in motor current ripple and audible noise.
- Shortening the dead time from 100 ns to 50 ns saves about 0.3 W.

### 2.1 Totals per channel at 80 A

$$
P_{ch}=P_{cond}+P_{sw}+P_{shunt+Cu}\approx21.5+2.7+5.1=\mathbf{29.3\ W}
$$

- All four channels at burst: **P_tot ≈ 117 W**.
- A realistic quad burst of 4 × 50 A gives P ∝ I² + linear terms, so P_tot ≈ 4·(8.4 + 1.7 + 2) ≈ **48 W**.

Efficiency at burst, per channel: input power ≈ 25.2 V × 80 A × D. At D ≈ 0.8, P_in ≈ 1.6 kW, so loss ≈ 1.8%.

## 3. Thermal Model

### 3.1 Two-node RC network

```
Tj ──Rθ,j-b(1.5 K/W)── T_board ──Rθ,b-a── T_amb
 │                         │
C_die (~0.05 J/K)       C_board
```

**Board heat capacity.** One copper layer: 0.037² m² × 70 µm × 8960 kg/m³ = 0.86 g.

| Element | Mass | c_p | Heat capacity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Copper, 6 layers | 5.1 g | 0.385 J/g·K | 2.0 J/K |
